en: Vimānavatthu:
Purisavimāna,
Pāyāsivagga
3. The Mansion of the Fruit-Giver “High is this celestial mansion with its jeweled pillars,
extending sixteen yojanas in every direction.”
Seven hundred lofty gabled chambers,
beautiful with pillars of beryl and adorned with silver, are there;
therein you eat, drink, and enjoy yourself.
And divine lutes resound with sweet melody;
there are eight times eight well-trained,
beautiful celestial maidens, noble daughters of the Thirty-Three Gods.
They dance, sing, and rejoice.
You have attained divine power and great majesty;
what merit did you perform while being a human?
“By what means have you come to possess such blazing majesty,
and why does your complexion illuminate all directions?
That son of the gods, being delighted, [replied:]
"The giver of fruit obtains abundant fruit; this is the fruit of that action."
With a mind full of faith toward those who give uprightly,
he indeed rejoices when gone to heaven among the Thirty-three gods,
and he experiences the vast fruit of his merit.
To you alone, O Great Sage,
did I give four fruits.
Therefore, indeed, it is sufficient to give fruit.
A person constantly seeking happiness—
whether aspiring for celestial joys or desiring the highest excellence among humans.
"Because of that, my complexion is such as this...
and my complexion shines forth in all directions."
The third [chapter] is the Phaladāyaka-vimāna.
